summary.short: Connecticut Public Act 25-113 amends the state's Data Privacy Act and adds minors' online protections, social media safety duties, affordable broadband and related consumer rules, mostly applying from 1 July 2026.
summary.long: Public Act 25-113 (SB 1295), approved 24 June 2025, amends the Connecticut Data Privacy Act and adds unrelated provisions. Sec. 1 (from 1 July 2025) creates a Net Equality Program: qualified broadband providers must offer eligible households affordable service capped at $40 monthly, and state agencies must prefer such providers. Sec. 4 requires social media owners to add online safety centers and cyberbullying policies. Secs. 5-12 (effective 1 July 2026) amend the privacy act: applicability at 35,000 consumers or sensitive data, rights including opt-out of legal-effect profiling, minimization and consent duties, privacy notices disclosing large-language-model training, opt-out signals, processor contracts, and data protection and profiling impact assessments. Secs. 13-18 add minors' rules on account deletion, targeted advertising, sale, profiling, geolocation, design features and direct messaging. Sec. 19 requires vehicle providers to act on survivors' requests within two business days. Secs. 2-3 (lottery licensing, sports wagering voids) and 20-22 (automatic renewal, dealer fees, home-improvement advertising) add further consumer and gaming rules.
